newsitem.title: FINLAND: NESTE SAYS IN TALKS TO SELL BOREALIS STAKE.
newsitem.headline: NESTE SAYS IN TALKS TO SELL BOREALIS STAKE.

text.p: Finnish oil and energy group Neste Oy's president and chief operating officer Jukka Viinanen said on Wednesday the company was in talks with potential buyers of its 50 percent stake in polyolefins company Borealis.
Viinanen declined comment when asked whether Neste was in talks with Abu Dhabi's International Petroleum Investment Company (IPIC), part of the country's national oil company (ADNOC).
"I cannot confirm that and we don't want to make any comment on that ... I can confirm that talks are underway with potenial buyers," Viinanen told Reuters by telephone.
An Abu Dhabi government-owned newspaper said on Wednesday that IPIC was moving to buy Neste's 50 percent stake in Borealis.

"Substantial progress has been made by IPIC in its quest to acquire a 50 percent stake in the Scandinavian petrochemical firm Borealis from Finland's Neste Oy," the English-language Emirates News paper said.
"Negotiations have reached the point where IPIC will be going ahead with the buy-out," the paper quoted an unamed industry source as saying.
However, "a lot of the fine print of the agreement has yet to be agreed up," the same source told the paper.
Neste has ealier said it is prepared to sell its stake in Borealis which it owns 50-50 with Norwegian Statoil A/S .
Asked whether there had been any changes in Neste's plans to divest its Borealis stake, Viinanen said: "There has been no reason to change our course in that matter."
Borealis is the biggest polyolefins producer in Europe and the fifth largest in the world.
